text:
leo: Heads up — during the 02:30 east2 nightly training runs we're seeing intermittent packet loss between GPU nodes. Training pods hit RPC timeouts and a handful of parameter-sync failures. Seen across ~6 nodes in the cluster, ~1-3% of requests failing, spikes last 10-30s.

infra-bot: [alert] cluster-east2/gpu-pool: increased pod network error rate (3.1%) at 02:32 — alert-id: NET-1797

sarah.w: Which overlay are we running there? vxlan/geneve? Any recent kernel or firmware rollouts?

leo: Antrea in encap mode, Geneve overlay (6081). No infra kernel updates this week, but a small NIC firmware push two weeks ago to a subset of racks. Problem correlates with pods scheduled on those racks.

ajay.k: Can you grab a quick tcpdump and iperf between two problem nodes? Also run ethtool -k on the physical NIC. Might be GSO/GRO/TSO offload causing reassembly drops on encap.

leo: tcpdump (truncated) from node-gpu-07 when issue hit:
```
12:32:14.123456 IP 10.10.7.12.443 > 10.10.3.45.49152: Flags [P.], seq 1:1420, ack 1, win 32768, length 1419
12:32:14.123457 IP 10.10.3.45.49152 > 10.10.7.12.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:1200, ack 1420, win 65535, length 1199
(retransmit)
12:32:14.153000 IP 10.10.7.12 > 10.10.3.45: UDP, length 1500
12:32:14.153001 IP 10.10.3.45 > 10.10.7.12: UDP, length 1500

iperf3 short run between the two nodes: jitter 3-10ms, 1-2% packet loss on UDP test (reproducible).
```

sarah.w: tcpdump shows retransmits and some 1500B UDP frames getting through the encapsulation. What's the node MTU and geneve device mtu?

leo: Node MTU: 9000. antrea-gw (geneve) mtu: 8972. Underlay link MTU: 9216 on the leaf. But seeing fragmented UDP on the wire sometimes.

ajay.k: Post ethtool -k output for the NIC (eth0). I've seen offload bugs where GSO combined with encap causes kernel to hand over a big skbuff that the NIC can't handle and packets get dropped. Also check tx checksums and UDP fragmentation offload flags.

leo: ethtool -k eth0 snippet:
```
segmentation-offload: on
tcp-segmentation-offload: on
large-receive-offload: on
generic-segmentation-offload: on
udp-fragmentation-offload: on
```

maria_g: That udp-fragmentation-offload bit is suspicious. On Mellanox/Broadcom boxes we've seen a firmware bug where UDF+GSO+encap makes small fragments disappear. Last time we disabled GRO/GSO on the tunnel interface and it mitigated the flaps. Also check conntrack table exhaustion during the spikes.

leo: Quick test: disabled udp-fragmentation-offload and gso on eth0 on a single affected node:
```
ethtool -K eth0 ufo off gso off gro off tso off
```
Result: within one minute the node's training pods stopped hitting RPC timeouts. CPU on node increased a bit but stability returned.

ajay.k: Good quick mitigation. Longer-term we should: 1) test kernel/firmware update on a staging rack; 2) coordinate with NIC vendor if it's firmware; 3) consider disabling encap offloads in Antrea or flip to direct routing for GPU pool. Also capture BPF drop stats on the host.

maria_g: For RDMA-enabled cards: confirm whether RDMA is in use on those nodes. RDMA and encap can interact if driver paths share resources. If RDMA is active, we might need vendor involvement before toggling offloads globally.

leo: These nodes are mixed — some have RDMA left enabled for dataset ingest jobs. I'll isolate an RDMA node and run the same ethtool/gso toggle test and report.

oncall-ng: Please open an incident jira and schedule a rolling maintenance window for gpu-pool east2. We should avoid mass restarts until we validate firmware.

infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-3269: "east2 overlay packet loss affecting gpu training" — link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-3269 (assigned to eng-sre)

leo: Next steps I'm proposing:
- Roll mitigation across affected rack nodes: ethtool -K eth0 ufo off gso off gro off tso off (daemonset + node init script)
- Run staged kernel + NIC firmware on one rack and monitor 24h
- Add Antrea config change to disable encap offload on the Geneve iface as a fallback
- Vendor follow-up if firmware clearly correlates

sarah.w: Can you post the small patch for the node init script so we can review before applying? Also include a perf baseline for CPU impact.

leo: Will do. Pushing a short config now to the PR for review. TL;DR: mitigation works, looks like offload/encap interaction. Scheduling maintenance this afternoon for targeted racks. :) :thumbsup:
